purpose: SPARC64 firmware cpuid -> possible construction -> IRQ-stack/per-CPU/bringup consumption chain; legal cpumask width precondition and stage; real-boot/tool feasibility

case.mainline_checked: df2908090cda368b01ff43709f51890076c56157 (v7.3-rc2); record_one_cpu and setup_arch ordering unchanged relative to fixed

prior_material: cpu_identity_contract_20261021 used NR_CPUS=8 (NR_CPUS<=BITS_PER_LONG branch, small_cpumask_bits=NR_CPUS) and stopped at public re-bounding; it explicitly left multi-word/dynamic bitmap branches uncovered
new_question: sparc64 Kconfig default NR_CPUS=4096 selects the branch where small_cpumask_bits=nr_cpu_ids; weight and for_each_cpu then depend on the current runtime nr_cpu_ids. Does the same original code produce different possible sets and consumer coverage under that branch?

feasibility_findings_before_execution.qemu_upstream_v8_2_2_sun4u: hw/sparc64/sun4u.c lines 813 and 841: mc->max_cpus = 1 (XXX for now)
feasibility_findings_before_execution.qemu_upstream_v8_2_2_niagara: loads 1up-md.bin / 1up-hv.bin single-CPU images; no max_cpus override
feasibility_findings_before_execution.consequence: no multi-CPU sparse-cpuid SPARC64 guest is available through QEMU 8.2.2; a single-CPU boot cannot exercise the relation; qemu-system-sparc and gcc-sparc64-linux-gnu are not installed (apt candidates exist)
feasibility_findings_before_execution.fetch_note: raw upstream files fetched by curl into WSL /tmp only for reading; Ubuntu binary not installed, not identity-checked

method: host C projection that #includes original function bodies extracted verbatim from the pinned Git blobs; explicit stand-ins for cpumask/bitmap/memblock/printk with two compile-time width branches
stages_observed: IRQ stack allocation set (alloc_irqstack_bootmem, inside setup_arch, before setup_nr_cpu_ids)
bringup over present mask (cpuhp_bringup_mask) and cpu_up possible check

researcher_relations.R1_no_invented_identity: possible is a subset of provided cpuids
researcher_relations.R2_count_limit: when nr_cpus=L is given, |possible| <= L (kernel-parameters.txt nr_cpus text)
researcher_relations.R3_preserve_without_truncation: when |provided| <= L (or no L), possible equals provided
researcher_relations.R4_irqstack_before_online: every CPU brought online has hardirq/softirq stacks allocated (set_hardirq_stack dereferences hardirq_stack[smp_processor_id()])
researcher_relations.R5_percpu_before_online: every CPU brought online has a per-CPU offset assigned

not_claimed: no real SPARC boot, firmware, or hardware
no claim that every input/limit combination is a legal machine configuration
bringup stand-in only models the cpu_up possible check and online marking; no secondary CPU execution, IPIs, idle threads, or interrupt delivery
any fixed-version violation is a source-projection candidate requiring real-platform or maintainer confirmation, not a confirmed Linux defect
case was already read; this is not independent detection
stop_rule: first-run compile or execution failures are recorded, not silently fixed; any corrected rerun is recorded as a separate attempt
